member.name: T:ReactiveUI.Binding.BindingAffinity
member.summary:
Common affinity scores shared by binding type converters, property observation factories, command binders, and the source generator's observation/command plugins. A higher value indicates a stronger match; zero means the candidate does not apply.
, , and carry the same values as ReactiveUI's scores of those names; the platform-specific scores are this library's own.

member.summary: A value a two-way binding moved, and which side of the binding produced it.

member.name: T:ReactiveUI.Binding.BindingErrors
member.summary: How a binding reacts when the sequence feeding its write faults.
member.remarks: A faulted write has no caller stack to surface on: it arrives on whichever thread raised the change notification. Every fault is logged against the bound expression. A fault that carries an inner exception, a setter that threw, is rethrown as a . A fault with none is the sequence itself ending in error, and is only logged. Completion is ignored.

member.name: T:ReactiveUI.Binding.BindingHooks
member.summary: Lets a registered inspect, or refuse, a binding as it is created.

remarks.para: A hook is consulted once per binding, before anything is wired, and a hook that returns false cancels the binding outright. Hooks are registered with the service locator, so the set is only known at run time.
The locator is read on first use and the hooks are cached until is called. is the guard a caller tests first, so a binding builds the property-chain closures needs only when a hook exists.

member.name: F:ReactiveUI.Binding.BindingHooks.Gate
member.summary: Guards while it is (re)resolved.
member.remarks: Only the first resolve after a refresh takes it. Holding it while the locator is read stops a resolve that races from publishing the set that refresh dropped.

member.name: F:ReactiveUI.Binding.BindingHooks._hooks
member.summary: The resolved hooks, or null while none has been resolved yet.

member.name: P:ReactiveUI.Binding.BindingHooks.Any
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether any hook was registered when the hooks were last read.
member.remarks: Test this before building the arguments to : the closures they need cost more than the check, and are wasted whenever the answer is false.

member.name: T:ReactiveUI.Binding.IBindingFallbackConverter
member.summary: Converts runtime type pairs that no typed converter covers. The converter service asks the fallback converters only when no typed converter with a positive affinity is registered for the pair.
member.remarks: Affinity only ranks fallback converters against each other, and the earliest registered converter wins a tie. The library registers no fallback converters of its own.

member.name: M:ReactiveUI.Binding.IBindingFallbackConverter.GetAffinityForObjects(System.Type,System.Type)
member.summary: Calculates affinity for the specified runtime type pair.
member.param: The runtime source type.
The target type.
member.returns: A positive value when the converter handles the pair, where a higher value wins over other fallback converters; zero or less when it does not.

remarks.para:
This method MUST be:
Pure (no side effects)
Fast (cache any expensive metadata)
Safe (no exceptions, no user code execution)
This method is invoked during converter selection and may be called frequently. Results should be cached internally where appropriate.

member.name: M:ReactiveUI.Binding.IBindingFallbackConverter.TryConvert(System.Type,System.Object,System.Type,System.Object,System.Object@)
member.summary: Attempts to convert the value to the target type.
member.param: The runtime source type (guaranteed non-null).
The value to convert (guaranteed non-null).
The target type (guaranteed non-null).
Implementation-defined conversion hint (e.g., format string, culture).
The converted value. Implementations must produce a non-null value when returning .
member.returns: if conversion succeeded; otherwise, .

remarks.para: Returning obliges an implementation to produce a non-null , but that obligation is not expressed as a nullability annotation: implementations come from outside the library and nothing enforces it. The dispatch layer therefore checks, and reports a null result as a failed conversion rather than letting it reach a binding.
Null input handling is performed by the dispatch layer. This method will never receive null as the parameter.

member.name: T:ReactiveUI.Binding.ObservableAsPropertyAttribute
member.summary: Marks a partial, get-only property as backed by an . The source generator writes the property's body and a helper field named _{name}Helper, which you assign with ToProperty.

remarks.para: The property has to be declared by you, as a partial property, so every generator in the build can see it. A property only another generator writes is invisible to this one, so it could not be observed or bound.

The attribute is also accepted on a field, a method or an observable property, the forms ReactiveUI's older source generator supported. Nothing is generated for those. An analyzer reports each one and offers a code fix that rewrites it as a partial property. and exist for that rewrite.

member.name: T:ReactiveUI.Binding.ObservableAsPropertyHelper`1
member.summary: Backs a read-only "output property" with an observable. The property reports each new value through the change callbacks it was created with, so the owning object can raise its own change notifications.
member.typeparam: The type of the property value.

remarks.para: This helper is normally created by ToProperty, whose generated code supplies callbacks that raise the owning object's change notifications for the named property. It can also be created directly with callbacks of your own.

Values equal to the previous value are skipped. With no scheduler, or with the immediate one, each value is delivered on the thread that produced it. A value produced while another is being delivered waits for that delivery to finish, so the callbacks never run concurrently and never nest.

member.name: T:ReactiveUI.Binding.CommandBinding.CommandInvoker
member.summary: Executes a command with each value a sequence produces.

remarks.para: What an InvokeCommand does once the command is in hand, whether the generator resolved the command property at compile time or the runtime engine read it from the expression. Both hand the command here rather than writing the gating themselves, so a generated call site emits one call and the two paths cannot drift.

is asked at each emission rather than tracked from : the value being offered is the command parameter, so only the command can answer for that value, and an answer tracked from the event would have to be recomputed per value anyway. A value the command refuses is dropped rather than held.
An error from a source sequence is rethrown on the thread that raised it, and completion is ignored.

member.summary: Executes one command with each value the sequence produces, skipping values the command refuses.
member.typeparam: The type of the value offered as the command parameter.
member.param: The sequence driving the executions.
The command to execute.
member.returns: A disposable that, when disposed, stops executing the command.
member.exception: or is null.

member.name: M:ReactiveUI.Binding.CommandBinding.CommandInvoker.Invoke``1(System.IObservable{``0},System.IObservable{System.Windows.Input.ICommand})
member.summary: Executes whichever command the observed sequence of commands last produced.
member.typeparam: The type of the value offered as the command parameter.
member.param: The sequence driving the executions.
The command to execute, as the observed property produces it.
member.returns: A disposable that, when disposed, stops executing and stops observing the property.
member.exception: or is null.

remarks.para: The commands are subscribed first, so a command the sequence produces on subscription is latched before any value can arrive. Subscribing in the other order drops a value produced immediately.

A null command - a property not yet assigned, or a path through an absent parent - drops the values offered while it stands, and a later command picks up from the next value. Replacing the command executes nothing by itself: values are what drive an execution, which is why the two sequences are not combined.

member.name: T:ReactiveUI.Binding.Fallback.RuntimePropertyRaiser
member.summary: Raises one property's change notifications on one object, found by reflection.
member.remarks:
The runtime twin of the generator's raise plugins, for ToPropertyUnsafe. It looks for members in the order the generator does: ReactiveUI's raise extensions for an IReactiveObject, then a raise method, preferring one that takes event args, then the field behind a field-like event. A type can only raise its own events, so the raise method may be protected or private and the event field is always private; reflection reaches them where generated code would add an accessor to a partial type.
The members found for a type are cached. A raise method is bound to its owner as a delegate once, when the raiser is created, and each raiser caches its event args, so raising a value neither looks anything up nor allocates.

member.name: T:ReactiveUI.Binding.IInteraction`2
member.summary: Represents an interaction between collaborating application components.
member.typeparam: The interaction's input type.
The interaction's output type.

remarks.para: Interactions allow collaborating components in an application to ask each other questions. Typically, interactions allow a view model to get the user's confirmation from the view before proceeding with some operation. The view provides the interaction's confirmation interface in a handler registered for the interaction.

Interactions have both an input and an output. The interaction's input provides handlers the information they require to ask a question. The handler then provides the interaction with an output as the answer.
Through this interface, asks the question as an observable. On itself, returns a task and returns the same observable.

member.name: T:ReactiveUI.Binding.Interaction`2
member.summary: Represents an interaction between collaborating application components.
member.typeparam: The interaction's input type.
The interaction's output type.

remarks.para: Interactions allow collaborating components in an application to ask each other questions. Typically, interactions allow a view model to get the user's confirmation from the view before proceeding with some operation.
By default, handlers are invoked in reverse order of registration. That is, handlers registered later are given the opportunity to handle interactions before handlers that were registered earlier.

Note that handlers are not required to handle an interaction. They can choose to ignore it, leaving it for some other handler to handle. The interaction's method will throw an if no handler handles the interaction.

member.name: T:ReactiveUI.Binding.ObservedProperty
member.summary: Observes properties for code that another source generator writes, with the behaviour of WhenAnyValue and without a generated binding.

remarks.para: A source generator never sees another generator's output, so code a generator writes cannot rely on this library's generator to bind a WhenAnyValue call. These methods take what that generator would have read from the call: the property as a lambda, and a delegate that reads it. They use no reflection, and are safe to trim and to publish ahead of time.
Hand-written code calls WhenAnyValue instead, which the generator binds.

The family observes one property, two properties, or two properties through a selector. continues a path one property further, so x => x.A.B is Create(source, x => x.A, x => x.A).Then(a => a.B, a => a.B). follows a property that holds an observable, as WhenAnyObservable does.

member.summary: Extension methods for binding an observable stream directly to a target property (BindTo). These generic stubs throw when no concrete generated overload is found; the source generator emits concrete typed overloads that C# overload resolution prefers over these generic stubs.
Resolves a BindTo expression by reflection, for a call site the generator could not read.
member.remarks: The opt-in half of BindTo. member.summary: Extension methods that execute a command with each value an observable produces (InvokeCommand).
member.remarks: The command is offered every value the sequence produces, as the command parameter, and a value the command refuses is dropped. A ReactiveCommand is reached through these overloads like any other : the parameter is passed as rather than the command's input type.
member.summary: Resolves an InvokeCommand expression by reflection, for a call site the generator could not read.
member.remarks: The opt-in half of InvokeCommand. The unsuffixed overload resolves at compile time and throws when no generated dispatch claimed the call site; this one walks the chain by reflection instead, and is annotated so a consumer publishing trimmed or ahead-of-time sees the requirement at their own call site.
member.summary: Extension methods that turn an observable into the backing store of a read-only property (ToProperty). These generic stubs throw when no concrete generated overload is found; the source generator emits concrete typed overloads that C# overload resolution prefers over these generic stubs.
Backs a read-only property with an observable, resolving the property and its notifications by reflection.
member.remarks: The opt-in half of ToProperty, for a call site the generator could not read: a property named by a string that is not a constant, or a source type whose notifications generated code cannot raise. These read the property name and find the members that raise its notifications at run time, and are annotated so a consumer publishing trimmed or ahead-of-time sees the requirement at their own call site.

member.summary: Observes property chains that are only known as expressions at run time.
member.remarks:
These overloads take an the caller built rather than a lambda the compiler can read, so no generator resolves them: the chain is always walked by reflection, and the overloads are annotated as not trim- or AOT-safe.
The chain walking is the engine the runtime observation fallback uses: it resolves each link, re-subscribes a deeper link when an intermediate value changes, and filters duplicates. Each arity differs only in how many chains it combines.

member.name: M:ReactiveUI.Binding.ReactiveUIBindingExtensions.Chains``1(``0,System.Object,System.Boolean,System.Linq.Expressions.Expression[])
member.summary: Subscribes to every chain an overload was handed, after refusing a missing argument.
member.typeparam: The type of the object the chains are rooted on.
member.param: The object the chains are rooted on.
The projection the caller supplied, which is required.
Whether a chain reports only when its value changes.
The expressions naming the chains.
member.returns: One observation per chain, in the order the chains were given.
member.remarks: Every arity funnels its argument checks and its subscriptions through here, so each overload is the signature and nothing else. The array is built once when the observable is created rather than per notification, so a higher arity costs one allocation at subscription and nothing while it reports.

member.name: T:ReactiveUI.Binding.ObservableForProperty.ExpressionChainSink`2
member.summary: Observes the leaf of an expression member chain (x.A.B.C) and emits its value as an observed change each time any link changes.
member.typeparam: The root sender type surfaced on the emitted change.
The leaf value type.
member.remarks: Each link is observed on the value the previous link produced, and the deeper links are re-attached when an intermediate value changes. The current leaf value is emitted on subscribe unless the first value is skipped. Nothing is emitted while an intermediate value is null. A leaf value that is not a faults the observer with an . The sequence never completes; observed values carry the root object as their sender.

member.name: F:ReactiveUI.Binding.ObservableForProperty.ReactiveNotifyPropertyChangedMixins.NotifyFactoryCache
member.summary: MRU cache that maps (sender type, property name, before-change flag) to the best implementation for that combination.
member.remarks: The entry is supplied through the context argument rather than looked up here, so only a resolution that actually found an implementation is ever stored. A failure is deliberately not stored: the locator can still be empty the first time a property is observed — an observation running ahead of application startup, or a test suite whose registration belongs to a later test — and a stored failure would outlive the registration that fixes it, leaving that sender and property permanently unobservable.

member.name: T:ReactiveUI.Binding.Observables.EventObservable`1
member.summary: Emits a value on subscribe, then again each time an event is raised.
member.typeparam: The type of the property value.
member.remarks: The value comes from the getter, which is read on subscribe and on every raise, so the event's arguments are ignored. The value read on subscribe is always emitted. When distinct filtering is on, a later value equal to the last emitted one is dropped. A getter that throws on subscribe makes Subscribe throw after the handler is detached, and one that throws while the event is raised propagates to whoever raised it. The sequence never completes.

member.summary: Default implementation of that resolves views for view models using a three-tier resolution strategy: source-generated AOT-safe dispatch, explicit runtime mappings, and service locator fallback.

member.name: M:ReactiveUI.Binding.DefaultViewLocator.SetGeneratedViewDispatch(System.Func{System.Object,System.String,ReactiveUI.Binding.IViewFor})
member.summary: Adds a source-generated view dispatch function. Called by __ReactiveUIGeneratedBindings: from a module initializer in a C# 9 or newer project, and from its static constructor in an older one. Each assembly that contains views registers its own.
member.param: The dispatch function that resolves views by type-switching on the view model instance.
member.remarks: Every registered function is consulted, the most recently registered first, and the first view it returns wins. A view model that two assemblies both have a view for therefore resolves to the view of the assembly that registered last. Registering a function that is already registered has no effect.

member.name: M:ReactiveUI.Binding.DefaultViewLocator.ResolveView``1
member.summary: Resolves a view for a view model type under the default contract, without a view model instance.
member.typeparam: The view model type.
member.returns: The resolved view, or when nothing maps or registers one.
member.remarks: The generated lookups dispatch on a view model instance, so without one this asks the explicit mappings and then the service locator. The view's ViewModel is left unset: there is no instance to give it.

member.name: M:ReactiveUI.Binding.DefaultViewLocator.ResolveView``1(System.String)
member.summary: Resolves a view for a view model type under a contract, without a view model instance.
member.typeparam: The view model type.
member.param: The contract to resolve under, or null for the default view.
member.returns: The resolved view, or when nothing maps or registers one.
member.remarks: The generated lookups dispatch on a view model instance, so without one this asks the explicit mappings and then the service locator. A mapping whose view does not implement for the type is skipped. The view's ViewModel is left unset: there is no instance to give it.

member.name: M:ReactiveUI.Binding.DefaultViewLocator.ResolveView(System.Object,System.String)
member.summary: Resolves a view for the view model using its runtime type, without building any type at run time.
member.param: The view model instance to resolve a view for.
The contract to resolve under, or null for the default view.
member.returns: The resolved view with its ViewModel set, or if no view is found.
member.remarks: This asks the source-generated lookups, then the mappings added with Map for the view model's runtime type. Both are safe in a trimmed or native AOT application. It never asks the service locator: a view registered there only as needs . When neither finds a view, a warning is logged that says so.

member.name: M:ReactiveUI.Binding.DefaultViewLocator.ResolveViewUnsafe(System.Object,System.String)
member.summary: Resolves a view for the view model using its runtime type, and falls back to the service locator through a type built at run time.
member.param: The view model instance to resolve a view for.
The contract to resolve under, or null for the default view.
member.returns: The resolved view with its ViewModel set, or if no view is found.
member.remarks: This runs first. When it finds nothing, this closes IViewFor<> over the view model's runtime type and asks the service locator for it. A native AOT application cannot build that type, so prefer a generated view or a Map registration.

member.name: M:ReactiveUI.Binding.DefaultViewLocator.TryResolveViaReflection(System.Object,System.String)
member.summary: The service locator tier of , which closes IViewFor<> with MakeGenericType.
member.param: The view model instance.
The normalized contract string.

member.remarks: Closing IViewFor<> over a runtime type needs the runtime to build an instantiation the compiler never saw, which an ahead-of-time build cannot do. member.param: The length of the collection.
member.returns: A tuple containing the start offset and the length of the range.
member.exception: The range falls outside a collection of elements.
